title: docs.devin.ai/llms-full.txt
snippet:
Devin has two pricing models:
* **Self-serve**: Free, Pro, Max, and Teams plans you can sign up for directly at [app.devin.ai](https://app.devin.ai). Self-serve usage is billed through a mix of included quota and on-demand credits. See [Self-serve plans](/admin/billing/self-serve) for full details.
* **Enterprise**: Devin Enterprise customers are billed in Agent Compute Units (ACUs) at the rate set in their order form. See [Enterprise](/admin/billing/enterprise) for how ACU consumption is tracked, or [contact sales](https://cognition.com/contact) for pricing.

## Manage budgets with the V3 API
All requests authenticate with an enterprise **service user token**. Callers need the **ManageAcuLimits** account permission or [delegated access](#who-can-manage-a-budget) to the budget. Use `https://api.devin.ai` as the base URL. See the [V3 API overview](/api-reference/v3/overview) for authentication and service user guidance.
Budget-scoped collection endpoints take the budget in the path: `/v3/enterprise/usage-policies/budgets/{budget_id}/...`. Endpoints that address a single tier or request (`/tiers/{tier_id}`, `/requests/{request_id}`) resolve the budget from the tier or request. On `/v3` they return HTTP `404` for an account-wide tier or request; those stay on `/v3beta1` (see [User-level ACU limits](/admin/billing/user-acu-limits)).

* **ChatGPT plans:** You can share a personal ChatGPT **Go**, **Plus**, or **Pro** plan with Devin. You cannot share a Free plan, or a Business, Team, or Enterprise workspace account.
* **Devin plans:** Token sharing is available on the [self-serve](/admin/billing/self-serve) **Pro**, **Max**, and **Teams** plans. It's not available on the Free plan or on Enterprise accounts. If you're on the Free plan, you'll see an **Upgrade your plan to connect ChatGPT** prompt in settings.

ChatGPT plans are linked per user, not per team. Each member of a Teams account can link their own ChatGPT subscription, and the sessions that member owns draw from their ChatGPT plan. There is no shared team-wide ChatGPT plan, and one member's linked plan is never used for another member's sessions. In a shared session, only the session owner can change the switch.

| Plan | For | Price | Members |
| - | - | - | - |
| **Free** | Individuals trying Devin | Free | 1 |
| **Pro** | Individual users | \$20/month | 1 |
| **Max** | Power users who need more quota | \$200/month | 1 |
| **Teams** | Teams working with Devin together | \$80/month | Multiple |

title: Plans, ACUs & What It Really Costs
snippet:
| Plan | Price | Included usage | Past the quota |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free | $0, one member | A light quota and limited models | Upgrade to a paid plan |
| Pro | $20/month, one member | A daily and weekly quota, with access to frontier models and Devin cloud sessions | Prepaid credits, billed at API pricing |
| Max | $200/month, one member | A much larger weekly quota with no daily cap | Same as Pro |
| Teams | $80/month minimum; $40/month per full seat | Each full seat gets a quota equal to Pro; free flex seats use only shared credits; up to 200 members | Shared credits for the whole team |
| Enterprise | Custom | ACUs at the rate in your order form, with SSO and dedicated or VPC deployment | Set by contract |

On Teams, the $80 minimum is met by full seats or, with fewer than two, topped up as prepaid credits the team shares.

Until April 2026, Devin billed self-serve usage in Agent Compute Units (ACUs). The Core plan was pay-as-you-go at $2.25 per ACU, and the Team plan cost $500 a month with 250 ACUs included.
On April 14, 2026, Cognition replaced ACUs for self-serve customers with included quotas, with extra usage “priced and billed in dollars rather than ACUs.” The old Core and Team plans went away. Free doesn’t keep Core’s no-minimum pay-as-you-go billing, and Cognition said Teams “lowers the entry point relative to the old $500/month Team plan.”

Devin doesn’t list a price per task. Its documentation says usage depends on the “number and complexity of actions Devin takes,” plus VM time and bandwidth, which are “typically a small fraction of total usage.” Beyond the quota, extra usage is billed at API pricing.

| Team plan | $80/month minimum; $40 per full seat; free flex seats use shared credits | $200+/month in $100 steps, including the same amount of workspace usage, shared by the team |
| Model usage | Included quota, then prepaid credits at API pricing | Billed by your own provider, through subscriptions or API keys |

title: Devin Pricing: Feature Breakdown & Is It Worth It in 2026?
snippet:
Devin AI pricing ranges from the **$20/month** Core plan. It suits small teams who need to integrate with Jira and Linear. Teams requiring API access will need to pay for the (steep) $500/month Teams Plan.

Devin offers a **$20/month** Core plan, a **$500/month** Team plan, and a **custom-priced** Enterprise plan.

At $20/month, the Core plan lets developers try Devin without committing to a $500 subscription. This plan suits **freelancers, individuals, and small teams** with light, low-ACU tasks. The pay-as-you-go model fits users with limited workflows,****offering additional ACUs at $2.25 each.

- **Ability to provide API/Secret keys:** The Core plan lets developers provide API and secret keys so Devin can access GitHub, cloud services, or third-party apps. This setup doesn’t use the Devin API, which is limited to Team and Enterprise plans. Core users cannot control Devin programmatically through an external API.

## **Team plan:** $500/month
At $500 per month, the Team Plan targets **medium-sized companies** needing an AI coding assistant for multiple projects. This subscription provides 250 Agent Compute Units (ACUs), and Devin sells Team Plan subscribers additional ACUs for $2 each.

- **Access to the Devin API for workflow automation:** Engineering teams get more control over how Devin fits into existing CI/CD systems. Through the API, teams can integrate Devin directly into their pipelines and automate repetitive workflows without manual oversight.

You’re an individual or **small team** that needs to automate lightweight tasks like bug fixes, small features, or AI-assisted prototypes. Keep in mind that Core plan users face limits, since ACUs can run out if too many tasks are executed.
### Choose the Team Plan if:
The Teams Plan fits **medium-sized companies or scaling organizations** managing multiple repositories, frequent pull requests, and collaborative projects. It suits teams needing predictable monthly ACUs and multiple sessions. Teams needing parallel session support and pull request creation or reviews also benefit from the Teams Plan.
